title: Search Quality Review
methodology_note: Google's Helpful Content guidance was verified fresh in this session (not carried forward from AQ-01): as of the current documentation, 'Helpful Content System' is no longer a standalone, separately-named ranking update — its signals were folded into Google's core ranking systems. E-E-A-T remains Google's current terminology. Source: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content. This review reuses AQ-01/AQ-01R/AQ-01R2's verified E-E-A-T and Helpful Content scores as its evidentiary baseline (re-deriving them from scratch here would be a re-estimate, the exact discipline this audit chain has repeatedly held itself to) and applies two lenses AQ-01 never assessed: internal competition between pages, and Google's current self-assessment framing specifically.

baseline_scores_reused.eeat_signals: 66 (documented as a slight undercount pending a formal AQ-01R3 rerun — see reports/aq-03-retraction-notice.md)

content_quality.question: Does the content provide original information, substantial value, and avoid being created primarily to attract search visits?
content_quality.assessment: Satisfies for the food-ontology tier post-AQ-02A: every leaf/group/category page opens with authored, non-templated narrative prose (1,252/1,252, TC-01 RESOLVED) and now carries an authored, entity-specific description in both the meta tag and JSON-LD (AQ-04B). Does not yet fully satisfy for the wine-education tier: the 'Why this category matters' noun-swap sentence and a leftover unedited template variable ('is the best if the dish is smoky for X') remain live and unresolved since AQ-01 — the single clearest content-quality gap left on the site, carried across every audit in this chain without remediation.

expertise.question: Is authorship clear and verifiable, with evidence of the expertise involved?
expertise.assessment: Organization schema (index.html, about.html) names the real operating entity (Albor Digital LLC) and the homepage's FAQPage content directly states 'Content is authored by Gustavo Aragones for Pairing Method, with chef-forward, educational intent' — a real, specific authorship claim, not a generic disclaimer. This is a genuine expertise signal Google's guidance explicitly asks for. Individual entity pages do not carry per-page byline/author markup — reasonable for a reference-work format (an encyclopedia entry doesn't need a byline the way a blog post does), consistent with Article schema correctly not being claimed for this content type (AQ-05C).

people_first_focus.question: Would someone leave this page feeling they'd learned enough to achieve their goal?
people_first_focus.assessment: For a food-entity page: yes, on the evidence available — a reader lands on genuine narrative (what the ingredient is, how it's used, wine pairing guidance, a beginner-friendly FAQ) before hitting any structured data table, per AQ-02A's explicit narrative-first architecture rule. For a dish-pairing page: partially — the pairing-matrix confidence scores ('Pairing Strength: 95%') remain unexplained (an AQ-01 Priority 3 finding, still open), which risks a reader trusting or dismissing a number they can't interpret.

internal_competition_analysis.framing: New lens AQ-01 did not apply: do multiple pages target the same search intent closely enough that they could cannibalize each other's ranking rather than both ranking well independently?
internal_competition_analysis.candidates_reviewed: The 8 unresolved canonical-identity variety-pairs from AQ-03 (reports/catalog-canonical-identity.json bucket C) are the site's only structurally-flagged candidates for this risk — pairs of entities sharing a common alternate name, which is exactly the shape of potential search-intent overlap.
internal_competition_analysis.spot_check_evidence: Sampled mandarin/clementine and lime/key-lime seo_description text directly: all four are specific, differentiated, non-templated (e.g., mandarin's is built around 'loose-skinned... salads, duck, holiday desserts'; clementine's around 'seedless winter citrus... honeyed sweetness... snacking'). This is not duplicate content by any measure — a search-quality evaluator would not flag these as near-duplicate pages.
internal_competition_analysis.conclusion: Differentiated content substantially reduces (but doesn't fully resolve) internal-competition risk for these 8 pairs. The residual question is not a content-quality defect but the same open editorial/canonical-identity question AQ-03 already surfaced and deliberately left unresolved: are these the same searchable concept users would expect one answer for, or genuinely distinct entities? This review adds evidence relevant to that future decision without making it — consistent with AQ-03's own discipline of not resolving culinary/botanical judgment calls by assumption.
internal_competition_analysis.pages_needing_consolidation: None identified with confidence. The 8 pairs above are candidates for a future review, not confirmed consolidation targets — their content is differentiated enough that consolidation is not obviously correct, and un-consolidating a wrongly-merged concept is harder than merging a wrongly-split one, so this review does not recommend action either way.

entity_clarity.assessment: Strong, on verified evidence: 0 duplicate canonical IDs across 1,166 entities (AQ-03), 0 duplicate canonical URLs across all published domains (AQ-05A), every DefinedTerm/DefinedTermSet identifier traces exactly to its catalog canonical id with 0 mismatches (AQ-04C). A search engine building an entity graph from this site has a clean, unambiguous 1:1 mapping between URL and concept for every published page except the 8 variety-pair candidates noted above.

internal_linking_assessment.assessment: Reused from verified evidence, not re-measured: 0 orphaned pages (AQ-02B4, reconfirmed AQ-05A), 0 unsupported relationships across 4,140 checked (AQ-02B3), every page reachable through 3 independent discovery paths (AQ-05B). From a search-quality perspective this matters because internal links are one of Google's own signals for understanding page importance and topical relationships within a site — a site with verified-complete internal linking gives Google a clean signal to work with, not a noisy or incomplete one.

search_intent_assessment.informational_intent: Well-served — every entity page answers 'what is X' before anything else, per the narrative-first architecture (AQ-02A).
search_intent_assessment.comparative_pairing_intent: Served for wine pairing (every entity carries pairing guidance) but the confidence-score presentation (unexplained percentages) may frustrate a reader trying to use the number, not just read prose around it — an open, previously-identified gap (AQ-01 Priority 3), not new to this review.
search_intent_assessment.navigational_intent: Well-served — domain hubs, /ingredients/ directory, and site search all independently verified complete (AQ-02B, AQ-05B).

pages_that_satisfy: Food-ontology leaf/group/category pages post-AQ-02A/AQ-04B — authored narrative, accurate structured data, specific non-templated descriptions.
The homepage — real Organization/authorship claims, a working (if now SERP-inert) FAQ section with genuine content.
pages_that_disappoint: Wine-education tier category hub pages carrying the noun-swap template sentence — the single most detector-visible template signature left on the site, unresolved since AQ-01.
Dish-pairing pages with unexplained 'Pairing Strength: XX%' scores and (per AQ-01R, still open) dead 'View Bottle' links.
overall_certification: PASS with 2 pre-existing, previously-documented open items carried forward (wine-tier templating, unexplained pairing scores) — neither newly discovered by this review, both already scoped in reports/content-quality-audit/recommended-improvements.md and explicitly out of AQ-05's scope (AQ-05 does not redesign publication).
